sections.label: Survey of mature PMEs
sections.summary: In a survey of 1,000 mature PMEs aged 40 and above, about one in two said tightening the employment pass quota in weak-hiring sectors will help protect their jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In our recent survey of 1,000 mature PMEs aged 40 and above, about one in two of them said that the tightening of the employment pass quota in sectors which have weak hiring practices of Singaporeans will help to protect their jobs.

sections.label: TAFEP powers and EP review
sections.summary: MOM should review the legal framework, give TAFEP expanded investigation, enforcement and punishment powers, and enhance EP review with a point system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Besides reviewing and publishing the "triple weak" watchlist which MOM and Tripartite Alliance Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) maintain, I submit that MOM should review the existing legal and policy framework and give TAFEP more teeth and bite through legislating expanded powers of investigation, enforcement and punishment against companies, employers and even individuals who discriminate in an employment context.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Second, we can level the playing field for local PMEs by enhancing the EP application review process to move beyond looking at the individual applicant's educational qualification and salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We can incorporate a point system, factoring in: one, support from sectoral tripartite expert committee; two, whether the employer has been investing in hiring and developing local workers; and three, diversity of nationalities.

sections.label: Enforcement, HR standards, EP process
sections.summary: The passage proposes stronger enforcement and penalties, giving TAFEP more teeth, improving HR standards, and enhancing the EP application process beyond qualifications and salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, we should have stronger enforcement and tougher penalties for errant employers and give TAFEP more teeth in investigation, enforcement and meting out penalties against these employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Second, we can strengthen fair employment through improving HR standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Third, we should also enhance the EP application process, looking beyond the education qualification and salary of the applicants.

sections.label: IPS-OnePeople.sg discrimination study
sections.summary: A 2019 IPS-OnePeople.sg study found almost 60% of Malays and 56% of Indians perceived discriminatory treatment at work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: An IPS-OnePeople.sg study in 2019 revealed that almost 60% of Malays and 56% of Indians perceived discriminatory treatment at work.

sections.label: ADB age discrimination report
sections.summary: About one in five Singaporeans experience age discrimination in their workplace, according to ADB's Global Workforce Review 2020 report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: About one in five Singaporeans experience age discrimination in their workplace, according to global payroll and human resources leader ADB’s new Global Workforce Review 2020 report.

sections.label: TAFEP fair consideration issue
sections.summary: TAFEP's FY2018/2019 annual report found the top issue was fair consideration for Singaporeans, with one in four feeling victims of preferential treatment to foreign counterparts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: According to TAFEP’s annual report for fiscal year 2018/2019, the top issue handled from 1 April 2018 to 31 March 2019 was fair consideration for Singaporeans, whereby one in four felt that they were victims of preferential treatment to their foreign counterparts.

sections.label: TAFEP powers and anti-discrimination laws
sections.summary: The speaker urges TAFEP to name errant employers, wants TAFEP given powers, and calls for whistle-blowing and anti-discrimination laws to protect Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: TAFEP should not shy away from naming the errant employers so that this can exert a strong pressure on the company, or the culprits in the company who are practising discriminatory practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: By giving TAFEP powers, this will hopefully send a stronger signal to trigger whistle-blowers who can provide leads to check on suspected companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I also urge trade unions to mobilise their members to whistle-blow and report suspect cases of discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the current global labour competition and economic climate likely to be sustained moving forward, Singapore needs to strengthen our measures, take a leaf out of other countries’ legislation on fair employment and hiring practices and look into anti-discrimination laws to protect our Singaporean workers and future workforce.

sections.label: Women's median salary gap
sections.summary: MOM data shows women earned a median salary of $342 less than men, even for the same type of job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Based on MOM’s data, women earned a median salary of $342 less than men, even those doing the same type of job.

sections.label: Marital status asked at recruitment
sections.summary: Eighty percent of female respondents said they were asked about their marital status at recruitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Eighty percent of female respondents said they had been asked about their marital status at the point of recruitment.

sections.label: Legislate Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment
sections.summary: The speaker asks for the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices to be legislated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Today, I only have one thing to ask.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And that is for us to legislate the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices.

sections.label: Legislating guidelines sends strong message
sections.summary: Legislating the guidelines would signal that workplace discrimination will not be tolerated and unfair practices will be punished by law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Most importantly, legislating the guidelines will send a loud and clear message to employers that discrimination in the workplace will not be tolerated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: It will be illegal and unfair practices will be punished by law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: It is time that our laws on workplace discrimination match the seriousness and pervasiveness of the problem.

sections.label: CCP training and salary support
sections.summary: CCPs provide up to 90% training and salary support to employers who hire and reskill mid-career jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: CCPs provide up to 90% training and salary support during the period of training to employers who hire and reskill our mid-career jobseekers.

sections.label: Job reskilling and placement efforts
sections.summary: Financial institutions committed to reskill and redeploy over 5,000 employees, and the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package placed more than 110,000 locals into opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For example, following the financial services JTM, financial institutions have committed to reskill and to redeploy more than 5,000 employees to take on new and enhanced roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have also ramped up employment facilitation efforts through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, placing more than 110,000 locals into jobs and skills opportunities as of end-April this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Within six months it supported 42,000 employers who hired more than 270,000 new local workers.

sections.label: Legislation on errant employers
sections.summary: Legislation could give more enforcement powers against errant employers, protect whistle-blowers and signal what society will not tolerate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Legislation could give us more enforcement powers against errant employers beyond suspending work pass privileges and it can confer better protection on employees who whistle-blow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It can also send a clearer signal on what we, as a society, will not tolerate as bad behaviour on the part of employers.

sections.label: Tripartite Committee on legislation
sections.summary: A Tripartite Committee is being set up to examine whether legislation is the best policy option, weighing potential ramifications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For example, if not properly designed, the legal framework could become overly onerous and inadvertently deter employers from setting up shop here and hiring the very groups that we seek to protect.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Nonetheless, we empathise with Singaporeans' concerns and apprehensions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, I am therefore setting up a Tripartite Committee to examine if legislation is the best policy option to advance on the gains that we have made.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Government, union and employer representatives will deliberate thoroughly whether legislation should be pursued, taking into consideration potential ramifications.
